title.zh: 看不清质量的时候：柠檬市场与保险
title.en: When Buyers Can't See Quality: Lemons and Insurance

desc.zh: 二手车市场为什么烂车多？保险为什么要免赔额、要体检？医保为什么要大家都参加？银行为什么宁可不借也不涨利率？这篇从期望和风险厌恶讲起：风险池化、柠檬市场、保险的死亡螺旋、免赔额菜单、信号、道德风险、信贷配给和信用分，八个可以动手的模型，最后是大数据定价、基因信息和医保参保规则的前沿。
desc.en: Why are used-car lots full of lemons? Why does insurance come with deductibles and medical exams? Why should everyone join public health insurance, and why will a bank refuse a loan rather than raise the rate? Starting from expected value and risk aversion: risk pooling, the market for lemons, the insurance death spiral, deductible menus, signalling, moral hazard, credit rationing and credit scores, with eight hands-on models, ending at the frontier of data-driven pricing, genetic information and enrolment rules.

title.zh: 风险厌恶与确定性等价：为什么买平均亏钱的保险
title.en: Risk aversion and the certainty equivalent: why buy insurance that loses on average

desc.zh: 怕风险的人愿意为确定多付钱，最多肯付的保费减去平均损失就是风险溢价。
desc.en: A risk-averse person pays extra for certainty; the most they would pay minus the expected loss is the risk premium.

zh: 保险明明亏钱为什么还买

title.en: The market for lemons and adverse selection

desc.zh: 买家看不清质量只能按平均出价，好货退出，平均变差，市场一轮轮萎缩。
desc.en: Buyers who cannot see quality offer the average price; good goods withdraw, the average falls and the market shrinks round by round.

zh: 二手车市场为什么烂车多

title.zh: 保险的死亡螺旋、强制参保与核保
title.en: The insurance death spiral, mandates and underwriting

desc.zh: 按平均定价赶走最健康的人，保费越涨越高；强制、补贴或按体检分档能打断它。
desc.en: Average pricing drives out the healthiest and premiums climb; mandates, subsidies or underwriting classes can break the spiral.

zh: 为什么体检后保费不同
医保为什么要连续参保

desc.zh: 全保贵、带免赔额便宜，两类人各选一份，用选择说出自己的风险；罗斯柴尔德—斯蒂格利茨模型。
desc.en: Full cover at a high price and a cheap plan with a deductible let each risk type reveal itself by its choice: the Rothschild–Stiglitz model.

zh: 保险公司为什么要免赔额
罗斯柴尔德斯蒂格利茨

title.zh: 信号：文凭、保修、口碑与花钱证明自己
title.en: Signalling: diplomas, warranties, reputation and costly proof

desc.zh: 知道得多的一方做一件冒充者做不起的事来证明自己——文凭、保修、品牌、认证、口碑；只要代价因人而异，哪怕这件事本身没用也能传递信息（斯宾塞模型）。
desc.en: The better-informed side proves itself by doing something too costly to fake: diplomas, warranties, brands, certification, reputation. If the cost differs by type, even a useless act carries information (Spence).

title.zh: 道德风险、自付比例与委托—代理

desc.zh: 一方的行为另一方看不见、而后果有人兜底时，人会少小心、多冒险——保险、雇佣、存款保险、救助都是；办法是让行动者自担一部分后果（委托—代理问题）。
desc.en: When one side cannot see the other's actions and someone else bears the consequences, people take less care and more risk, in insurance, employment, deposit insurance and bail-outs alike; the remedy is making the actor bear part of the outcome (the principal–agent problem).

title.zh: 信贷配给：银行为什么不随便放贷
title.en: Credit rationing: why banks refuse rather than raise rates

desc.zh: 高利率先赶走稳当的借款人，银行的期望回报会在某个利率后下降，于是宁可拒贷；斯蒂格利茨—韦斯模型。
desc.en: High rates drive out safe borrowers first, so the bank's expected return can fall beyond some rate and it rations credit instead: Stiglitz–Weiss.

zh: 银行为什么不随便放贷

title.en: Where a credit score comes from

desc.zh: 评分卡把过去的还款记录变成违约概率和分数，银行再定门槛；没有记录本身也是信息。
desc.en: A scorecard turns your repayment history into a default probability and a score, and the bank sets a cutoff; a thin file is information too.

title.zh: 大数据定价、基因信息与参保规则的前沿
title.en: Frontier: data-driven pricing, genetic information and enrolment rules

desc.zh: 看得越清螺旋越难转、高风险者越难投保：大数据杀熟条款、欧盟 AI 法、GINA、医保断保等待期。
desc.en: Seeing more stops spirals but prices out high risks: China's anti-price-discrimination rule, the EU AI Act, GINA and enrolment waiting periods.
